explanation:
## How the rule was found

**What changes.** In every pair, the only edit is 0 → 1. No other colour moves, and the grid keeps its size. So the task is to decide which 0-cells become 1.

**Region size is not the rule.** My first inspection recoloured only the largest connected region of 0s.
- Pair 2 matched exactly with 4-connectivity: its changed cells form one 4-connected region of 90 cells.
- Pairs 1 and 3 had 67 and 37 mismatches. The 8-connected version did not fix them either.

My second inspection mapped the changed cells. In pairs 1 and 3 they fall into many separate 4-connected regions, some of only 1 or 2 cells, while larger zero regions elsewhere stay 0. So the deciding property is not size.

**What the filled regions have in common.** The new colour is 1, and colour 1 already appears in every input. That suggests existing 1s act as seeds that "flood" the empty space they touch. I wrote a check for this, but my inspection turns had run out, so I could not run it. Instead I checked some cells against the printed grids:

- **Pair 3:**
  - The 3-cell top-right region (0,11), (0,12), (1,12) sits beside the input 1 at (0,10), and it fills.
  - The block (8,2)–(9,4) stays 0. It meets a filled cell only diagonally, at (8,3)–(7,4), and touches no 1 orthogonally. So connectivity must be 4-way.
- **Pair 1:**
  - The column of 0s at x=6, rows 5–10, ends next to the 1 at (11,6), and it fills.
  - The single 0 at (4,8) has 1s only on its diagonals, at (3,7) and (3,9), and it stays 0. So "touching" must also be orthogonal only.
- **Pair 2:**
  - The leftover zeros (5,0), (5,11) and (5,12) have no orthogonal 1 neighbour, and they stay 0.
  - The big region touches the 1 at (1,0), and it fills.

**Rule.** Every 4-connected region of 0s that is orthogonally adjacent to at least one input cell of colour 1 becomes 1. All other cells stay as they are.

Because this was only checked by hand on these cells, the program still has to be run against all three train pairs to confirm it.

**On the test input.** The input contains 14 cells of colour 1 spread across the grid. Each zero region that borders one of them, for example the zeros around the 1 at (2,8)/(2,10) or next to (7,0)/(7,3)/(7,5), floods with 1. Zero pockets enclosed only by other colours stay 0.

**Construction stages.**
1. Start from the input.
2. Fill each qualifying region in turn and emit after each one, so a learner sees one seeded flood at a time.
3. Emit the final grid.
